title: AMD vs. Nvidia. 1 Metric Proves Which Is the Best Stock.
detail:
AMD vs. Nvidia. 1 Metric Proves Which Is the Best Stock.
Keithen Drury, The Motley Fool
Wed, October 21, 2026 at 8:35 AM MST 5 min read
NVDA
AMD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The debate over whether Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) or Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) is the better GPU stock has raged on for ages. At the start of the artificial intelligence (AI) arms race in 2023, it was Nvidia all day. In 2026, that narrative shifted in AMD's favor as its stock has risen about 150%, well above Nvidia's comparatively tame 16% return.

But all of that is in the past; what matters more is what each one will do in the future. I think there's one metric that points to which stock will be the better performer, and it clearly favors Nvidia.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.
Nvidia's revenue growth is superior to AMD's

In 2026, AMD has made significant strides toward becoming more competitive in its product offerings. Several AI hyperscalers are starting to deploy more AMD products, which has caused many investors to assume that AMD is winning some ground in data centers versus Nvidia. But that's not the case.

During Q2, AMD's data center revenue rose 107% year over year to $6.7 billion, so clearly it's trending in the right direction. However, AMD has a much more diversified business than Nvidia, and right now, diversification is hurting AMD. Data center products are the only place to be right now, and AMD's 50% overall revenue growth rate to $11.5 billion shows just how slowly the other parts of its business are growing compared to data center.

Nvidia is a much larger company, and its data center business grew 117% to $89 billion in its most recent quarter. Nvidia is both larger and growing faster, so the AMD-catching-up thesis isn't entirely accurate. AMD may be getting to the point where it's somewhat even with Nvidia, but the AI community still prefers Nvidia hardware. Overall, Nvidia's revenue grew at a 106% pace to $96.2 billion.

Nvidia is still the stronger company overall due to its focus on data centers. With both AMD and Nvidia projecting that the AI build-out will last through at least 2030, we're still in the early stages of the massive spending spree. So, Nvidia's positioning will help it thrive as a company overall versus AMD. However, this isn't reflected in their valuations, and this is the metric that points to Nvidia being the far better buy.

AMD has a ton of growth baked into the stock price

If we utilize next year's earnings projections to value the companies, a clear pattern emerges.

Susquehanna expects "modest upside" to third-quarter semiconductor earnings and fourth-quarter guidance, citing AI demand and a continuing broader industry upcycle.

The firm raised its AMD price target to $620 from $550 and Qualcomm to $185 from $160, maintaining its ratings.

Susquehanna cut targets on Coherent and Onsemi, but maintained 'Positive' ratings on both.

Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) and Qualcomm Inc. (QCOM) saw their price targets raised by Susquehanna on Wednesday, while Intel Corp. (INTC) and Coherent Corp. (COHR) faced cuts as the firm revised its outlook for semiconductor stocks ahead of quarterly earnings.

Susquehanna expects "modest upside" to third-quarter earnings and fourth-quarter guidance, driven largely by artificial intelligence (AI) demand, while the broader semiconductor upcycle continues, according to The Fly.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

At the time of this writing, QCOM and AMD stocks were trading nearly 1% higher, while COHR was up more than 1%. Meanwhile, INTC shares were in the red.

AMD, QCOM And SKWS See Higher Targets

Susquehanna raised AMD's price target to $620 from $550, maintaining a 'Positive' rating. It also raised QCOM's target to $185 from $160 and Skyworks Solutions' (SWKS) target to $90 from $65, maintaining 'Neutral' ratings on both.

The revisions come as AMD expects third-quarter revenue of approximately $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million, representing roughly 41% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. AMD's second-quarter revenue rose 50% to $11.5 billion, including a 107% jump in data-center revenue to $6.7 billion, driven by demand for EPYC processors and Instinct graphics processing units.

Qualcomm, meanwhile, reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $9.9 billion in July and expects non-handset revenue growth, including data centers, to exceed 60% in fiscal 2027, compared with 24% in fiscal 2026.

COHR, INTC And ON Face Target Cuts

Susquehanna cut its price targets by 20% for ON stock, about 18% for COHR stock, 17% for WOLF and 9% for INTC. The firm maintained 'Positive' ratings on Onsemi and Coherent and 'Neutral' ratings on Wolfspeed and Intel, according to The Fly.

Coherent, which supplies optical technologies used in AI infrastructure, reported fiscal fourth-quarter (Q4) revenue of $2.05 billion and forecast fiscal first-quarter (Q1) 2027 revenue of $2.2 billion to $2.4 billion.

Intel, meanwhile, forecast third-quarter revenue between $15.8 billion and $16.8 billion after reporting 25% year-over-year growth in second-quarter sales.

title: AMD’s Data Center Business Is Finally Delivering Profits. Can MU’s Rival Sustain the Momentum?
detail:
AMD’s Data Center Business Is Finally Delivering Profits. Can MU’s Rival Sustain the Momentum?
Noor Ul Ain Rehman
Wed, October 21, 2026 at 8:25 AM MST 4 min read
AMD
Trade AMD on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:AMD) fastest-growing business is no longer the one most people associate with its name. In the June quarter, Data Center revenue reached $6.718 billion, overtaking the combined contributions of its PC, gaming, and embedded businesses. Two years of interest in AI accelerators have changed the balance of its accounts, and yet the segment includes EPYC server processors as well as Instinct GPUs, making it impossible to attribute all that growth to AI accelerator sales alone.

Is Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) One of the Top 10 Dividend Stocks to Buy According to Reddit?
Bull Case

The improvement is substantial and evident in the company's earnings. Data Center revenue rose from $3.240 billion a year earlier to 6.718 billion, while segment operating income reached $2.103 billion, reversing a $0.155 billion loss. AMD attributed stronger sales to demand for EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs. Its total quarterly revenue increased from $7.685 billion to $11.536 billion, with GAAP operating income reaching $1.990 billion after a prior-year loss of $0.134 billion. The company is recording operating profits from a business that was loss-making in the comparison period.

READ ALSO: What Jim Cramer Says About Advanced Micro Devices' (AMD) AI Opportunity

Its remaining operations offer a useful check on the breadth of that improvement. Client revenue increased to $3.062 billion from $2.499 billion, while Embedded revenue reached $0.977 billion from $0.824 billion. The less encouraging figure was Gaming, where sales declined from $1.122 billion to $0.779 billion. AMD's results therefore reflect diverging end markets rather than uniform strength across its portfolio.

New customer announcements add commercial context without replacing reported revenue. In July, AMD and Anthropic announced an agreement for deployment of up to two gigawatts of Instinct MI450 GPUs, with the first gigawatt scheduled to begin in the first half of 2027. Microsoft also announced plans to deploy AMD's Helios racks on Azure. These agreements establish intended deployments, but neither release assigns them realized revenue in the June quarter. Read more extensively about AMD's bull and bear case here.

Bear Case

The earnings comparison needs a qualification. Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:AMD) year-earlier quarter included $800 million in inventory and related charges tied to US export restrictions on MI308 data-center GPUs. Their absence contributes to the striking recovery in GAAP gross margin, from 40% to 54%.

Broadcom (AVGO) shares fell 11.2% from their recent high on October 7, 2026, to the close on October 20. The worst of the slide came on October 16, when the stock lost 4.5%, a decline that tempts some investors to buy and others to sell. Broadcom has fallen harder than this before, so how did the investors who bought those earlier falls do a year later?

Broadcom Shares Were Higher A Year After Past Falls

Since 2010, Broadcom has recorded nine sharp falls, with each representing a drop of more than 20% within about six weeks of trading. Seven of those declines happened over a year ago, and the shares traded higher a year later in all seven cases. The median gain over that year was 45%. The other two falls, in January and July 2026, remain too recent to judge.

Realizing that gain meant holding for a year. Along the way, the median buyer waited 275 days, about nine months, for that year's best price, a median 62.3% above the price on the day of the dip. Most buyers initially saw little further downside, as the median lowest close arrived 3.6% below the price on the day of the dip. Yet after the falls of May 2019 and March 2020, the shares slid more than 30% below that price before they recovered.
